title: Four O'Clock Prices
logline: Before dawn at a great wholesale vegetable market, lorries arrive all at once, prices change by the minute, and a trader juggles buyers, a phone and a scale until the rush breaks into sudden quiet.

object.note: Object 4 (identity not chosen) may appear subtly, for example among Chathura's things while he travels, waits or watches, only where it sits naturally in a real moment. Never staged, never the subject.

thread_in.thread: From a reservoir's slow, silent mud to a wholesale market where lorries arrive all at once and attention scatters as fast as prices change.

thread_out.thread: After the rush breaks into sudden quiet, a different kind of lostness: mangrove channels where every turning looks the same, and a fisher who reads the roots like streets.

requirements: A working wholesale market with a trader willing to be followed for a whole night

lesson.in_simple_terms: When everything arrives at once, attention scatters. The texts compare this restlessness to water ruffled by the wind, and name rushing and doing many things at once as moments when it tends to arise.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: බොහෝ දේ එකවර, හදිසියේ කරන්නට සිදු වූ විට, සුළඟට සෙලවෙන වතුර මතුපිටක් මෙන් සිත එක දෙයක නොරැඳී විසිරෙයි.
lesson.the_teaching: Restlessness (uddhacca) is the second of the two delusion-rooted minds. Pradeepika explains it through one-pointedness, the mind's power to stay with one object: when agitation breaks that power, it throws the mind's other qualities off course too, so the object cannot be taken in properly. Margaya notes that this restless mind sometimes arises in sudden situations, when doing many things at once, and when working in a hurry, and Pradeepika's image for it is a surface of water shaken by the wind.
lesson.how_the_film_shows_it: Lorries arrive together in the dark, prices are chalked and shouted and changed, and the trader handles several buyers, a phone and a scale at once, losing a count and starting it again. Then the rush breaks: a cup of tea, a swept floor, sleep on a sack. The viewer feels the scattering, and the stillness after it, in their own attention before anything is said.

key_terms.en: one-pointedness; the power to stay with one object

lesson.caution: Restlessness here is not a productivity problem to be fixed with a mindfulness tip, and the film shows the pressure of conditions, not a fault in the traders.
lesson.builds_on: Where the drowned town showed confusion lying still and hidden, the market shows its other face: a mind that cannot stay, shaken loose by everything arriving at once.
lesson.evidence_class: editorial interpretation grounded in cited source teaching
